title: Restore programmatic slash-command dispatch under --agent via the Skill tool
description: Split out of CAM-254. Since CAM-240 spawns the orchestrator under `claude --agent subagent-orchestrator`, the SlashCommand path is gone: SlashCommand is not a grantable tool at all (claude-code-guide confirmed against https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools.md, which has no SlashCommand entry; slash commands are an interactive message-parsing construct, not a callable tool). Consequence proven live during CAM-253/CAM-254: the orchestrator-side inject path for /cam-issue and /cam-review is effectively broken under --agent. When the orchestrator session is live, `cam issue`/`cam review`/`cam spec` inject the slash-command text into the orchestrator pane %0, but under --agent (a) it cannot be run via a tool (no SlashCommand tool) and (b) the injected text lands in the composer without submitting (CAM-200). We currently work around it by executing the skill deterministic step directly (e.g. `cam issue --file-local`, `cam spec --persist`), which is fine for issue/spec but leaves /cam-review with no orchestrator-side programmatic path. claude-code-guide points to the `Skill` tool as the grantable mechanism that executes a skill in the main conversation: if the cam /cam-* commands are exposed as skills (or a parallel skill entrypoint is added), the orchestrator could dispatch them programmatically via the Skill tool instead of the dead SlashCommand path. Scope to investigate: (1) whether the cam commands in .claude/commands/ can be exposed/duplicated as .claude/skills/ entries invokable via the Skill tool; (2) add Skill to the orchestrator tools: allowlist if adopted; (3) reconcile with the CLI thin-proxy design (send-keys inject) so there is exactly one sanctioned dispatch path per command, not two half-working ones; (4) decide per-command whether the deterministic CLI channel (cam issue --file-local, cam spec --persist) is the canonical path and the Skill/inject path is only for interview-style commands (/cam-review, /cam-spec grill). Related: CAM-254 (drop the dead SlashCommand entry), CAM-200 (send-keys composer no-submit), CAM-240 (spawn under --agent). This is a design/architecture investigation; likely needs a /cam-spec grill before it is plannable.
